cim: Orange adds €250m to Orange Ventures to back AI and cybersecurity startups
cim_eredeti: Orange adds €250m to Orange Ventures to back AI and cybersecurity startups
szoveg_eredeti:
Orange is giving its corporate venture arm, Orange Ventures, another €250m to invest in startups from 2027 to 2032. It announced the allocation at its OpenTech event in Paris on Tuesday. The new money takes the fund’s assets under management to nearly €500m.

Of the €250m, €200m will go to Europe and €50m to Africa and the Middle East. The fund will put more weight on AI and cybersecurity. It will also keep investing in cloud, business software, consumer digital services, fintech and digital health.

“At a time when artificial intelligence is accelerating and cybersecurity risks are increasing, Europe must be able to foster and scale up its own technology champions,” said Christel Heydemann, Orange’s CEO.

Orange Ventures has 40 active portfolio companies. Its release named four of its six unicorns. The full six are Airalo, Dataiku, Monzo, Raisin, Multiverse Computing and HappyRobot, an Orange spokesperson told TNW.

Several have been busy this year. Multiverse Computing, the Spanish AI company, targeted a $570m Series C in July. HappyRobot raised a $150m Series C in August for its enterprise AI agents. In September, Nubank’s owner was in talks to buy Monzo at up to £10bn.

More than half of the fund’s portfolio companies have partnership agreements with Orange, the company said.

Orange created Orange Ventures in January 2021 with a €350m allocation. It took over the portfolio of Orange Digital Ventures, the unit it replaced.
